dimension_grades.evidence: Project Alpha and Blockers & Risks sections are written as narrative prose paragraphs, not bullet points.
The Blockers & Risks section contains multi-sentence prose blocks rather than self-contained 1–2 line bullets.
'Resolve the database migration issue' and 'Figure out coverage for Jake's absence' appear in both Blockers & Risks and Next Steps.

Next Steps contains 7 bullets including items like 'Update the project tracker' and 'Schedule sync with Platform team' that could be folded into project-specific sections or omitted from a leadership update.
The email opens with 'Hope you had a good weekend! I wanted to give you a rundown...' — pleasantries and context-setting, not a status summary.
There is no single summary sentence capturing wins and timeline shifts; the update buries both across separate sections.
No line in the update explicitly signals whether the reader needs to act or not; the closest is 'Will keep you posted' which is vague.
There is no summary line at all, so no label (plain or otherwise) is present.
The draft uses 'pretty significant setback,' 'real problem,' and 'scrambling' to describe the database migration issue.
'could potentially push things back' is vague with no concrete estimate such as '~1 week.'
No date or timeframe is given for when the resolution path will be clear; the update only says 'Will keep you posted as we learn more.'
The update never explicitly states that the database issue or staffing gap does not require director intervention.
The draft contains no internet-style abbreviations or casual shorthand labels.
The closing uses 'Best regards' which is overly formal, and the opening pleasantry adds filler rather than approachable directness.
The verbose prose sections and alarm language ('scrambling,' 'real problem') suggest no calibration to a director who reads on mobile and needs calm, concise framing.
